name: Observation of the doubly charmed baryon Ξcc⁺⁺

significance.locator: arXiv:1707.01621 abstract (no single overall significance figure stated)
significance.note: The abstract does not state a single overall significance figure in sigma (it says 'a highly significant structure'); left null rather than guessed.

summary.plain: LHCb observed a baryon (a proton-like particle) containing two charm quarks, the Ξcc⁺⁺, as a highly significant structure in its data. The quark model predicts such particles; an earlier claim by the SELEX experiment for a related state was not seen by several other searches.
summary.technical: A highly significant structure in the Λc⁺K⁻π⁺π⁺ mass spectrum is identified as the weakly decaying doubly charmed baryon Ξcc⁺⁺; the mass difference m(Ξcc⁺⁺)-m(Λc⁺) is measured to be 1334.94±0.72(stat)±0.27(syst) MeV/c², giving m(Ξcc⁺⁺)=3621.40±0.72±0.27±0.14 MeV/c².

title: Observation of the Doubly Charmed Baryon Ξcc++
why_it_matters: The quark model predicts doubly charmed baryons; in most calculations the Ξcc masses lie between 3500 and 3700 MeV/c², and the measured Ξcc⁺⁺ mass is 3621.40 MeV/c². The paper describes a longstanding puzzle: SELEX reported a Ξcc+ state at 3519 MeV/c², which FOCUS, BaBar, Belle and an earlier LHCb search did not find (the paper notes these null results do not exclude the original observations because the production environments differ).
